output:
All done — the plan was executed end to end and verification passed. Summary:

**Files created** (in `/home/agent/workspace`):
- `messy_data.csv` — 12 rows of intentionally dirty data
- `clean_data.py` — stdlib-only cleaner (csv + datetime + statistics)
- `cleaned_data.csv` — the verified output

**What the cleaner fixed:**
| Problem | Result |
|---|---|
| Exact duplicate row (John Smith ×2) | Dropped → 11 rows |
| Missing/invalid ages (`,`, `abc`, `230`) | Filled with median (36) — 3 fills |
| Mixed date formats (ISO, DD/MM/YYYY, `2024.04.01`, "March 3, 2024"…) | All normalized to ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| Stray whitespace & inconsistent casing | Trimmed, names/cities title-cased, emails lowercased |
| Malformed email (`not-an-email`) | Blank, flagged in the summary |

**Verification asserts (all green):** 11 rows · every date ISO-formatted · every age an integer in 0–120 · no stray whitespace · no duplicate emails.

One thing worth knowing: I caught and fixed a mid-run issue where median-filled ages printed as `36.0` (float); the final output writes clean integers. Also note `carol king`'s date `2024.04.01` parses as April 1 — if your data ever mixes `DD.MM.YYYY` dot formats, that's an ambiguity to handle explicitly.
